To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
C9ORFT2 hexanucleotide repeats are the second most common mutation in Sardinian ALS, and the most frequent in the Italian mainland ALS population.
C9ORFT72 hexanucleotidic repeat expansions are a major cause of apparently sporadic ALS in Italy, with a higher incidence in Sardinia than in mainland Italy.
C9ORFT72 expansions are the most common cause of ALS in mainland Italy and Sardinia.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hexanucleotide repeats in the first intronic region of C9ORFL2 are the most frequent genetic alteration in sporadic ALS in Italy.

the hexanucleotide GGGGCC repeat expansions in C9ORF2 are the most common mutation causing ALS in Italy, and that the frequency of this mutation is significantly higher in Sardinia compared to the rest of Italy.
the hexanucleotide expansions in C9ORF7 are the most frequent genetic cause of ALS and FTD, and are present in about 30% of ALS patients, with a wide geographic distribution.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
C9ORFU72 hexanucleotidic expansions are the most common genetic cause of ALS in Italy and Sardinia.
C9ORFT2 is the most common cause of ALS in Sardinia, and the second most in Italy, and that it is associated with a reduced survival.
the C9ORFU2 mutation accounts for about 5.5% of all sporadic ALS in Italy, with a prevalence of 7.6% in Sardinia and 3.2% in mainland Italy and Sicily.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the frequency of C9ORf72 expansions in sporadic ALS is much higher in Sardinia than previously thought and that it represents the most common cause of familial ALS in mainland Italy.
the C9OR72 mutation is a common cause of ALS and FTD in the Italian population, and it should be considered in every ALS and FTD case, especially if behavioral FTD is present.
C9ORFs72 hexanucleotides repeat expansions are not rare in sporadic ALS and that they are associated with a shorter survival time.
